messages:
Alex: Quick sync on customer asks: they want reliable structured-output validation + a types-first TS client for function/tool calls. Can we scope a minimal ship for the next release?
Maria: Clarify: by 'types-first' do we mean full generic inference of tool arg shapes or just explicit typedefs for common surfaces?
Derek: Prefer explicit typedefs initially. Generics are nice but will blow up review time. Proposed minimal TS pattern:
```ts
export interface ToolCall<Args = Record<string, unknown>> {
  name: string;
  args: Args;
}
export type RerankInput = { query: string; candidates: string[] };
```
Derek: This lets consumers supply precise arg types when they want, without us overengineering.
Sara: Python counterpart: recommend TypedDict and example using pydantic for validation in apps. Example sketch: 
```py
class ToolArgs(TypedDict):
    customer_id: str
    limit: int

def call_tool(name: str, args: ToolArgs) -> dict:
    ...
```
Sara: Also suggest a tiny validation helper that checks structured output against a schema (jsonschema or pydantic) and returns a short error for docs.
Tyler: For launch we need 3 docs artifacts: typed TS defs, two runnable examples (chat+tool, embeddings lookup), and a clear changelog/migration note. Changelog must call out any breaking param renames.
Alex: Proposed minimal launch criteria (ship-safest):
- TS typedefs covering chat/completions + function calling + minimal rerank types
- Python examples with TypedDict + pydantic pattern for validation
- 2 runnable examples in examples repo (chat-tool-exec, embeddings-retrieval)
- Docs page: quickstart + migration snippet + structured-output guidance
- Changelog entry + release checklist
Maria: Timeline? If we only do typedefs + one example (chat-tool) can we target next sprint end?
Derek: Yes if work splits: I own TS typedefs + unit tests, Sara owns Python example + validation helper, Tyler drafts changelog and release notes, Maria handles customer comms and FAQ.
Sara: One more ask from support: include a small automated test harness in examples so customers can run examples locally without secrets. A mocked runtime for tool calls.
Derek: Agreed. Keep API surface for rerank minimal: { query, candidates } and return a ranked array of indexes or ids. No fancy scoring structs yet.
Maria: Decision: no advanced generics or inferred types for v0.9 — defer to v1.0. Keep surface small to reduce API review scope.
Tyler: I'll draft the changelog blurb. Proposed header: "SDK v0.9.0 1 typed function calls + structured-output guidance" with migration snippet showing old->new call shape.
Alex: Action items recap: Derek -> TS typedefs + PR; Sara -> Python examples + validation helper + test harness; Tyler -> changelog + release checklist; Maria -> customer comms + FAQ draft. Docs-bot: please add checklist.
docs-bot: Checklist created: ["TS typedefs", "Python examples", "examples test harness", "docs quickstart", "changelog entry", "release QA"]
Alex: Back in 7 days for sign-off. Ping on PRs. :thumbsup:
